column1: # comment: "Email alignments. EmailMessage is equivalent to schema:EmailMessage; the rest use skos:closeMatch (cross-type/loose) to schema.org, the Nepomuk Message Ontology (NMO), and SIOC. The reified MessageParticipant relator is canonical; flat from/to/cc/bcc and their schema.org/NMO counterparts are lossy projection shortcuts. Trust terms (RelayHop/AuthenticationResult/signatures) are canonical \u2014 no maintained external RDF vocabulary exists for them. MessageParticipantRole envelope/resent roles are also canonical \u2014 no external vocabulary covers them. threadSubject and subjectPrefix are canonical \u2014 no maintained external vocabulary exposes thread-level normalized subject or per-message prefix stripping. MessageKind and its individuals are canonical \u2014 no maintained external vocabulary covers DSN/ARF/MDN/auto-generated report kinds. priority, importance, precedence, autoSubmitted, readReceiptRequested, and dispositionNotificationTo are canonical \u2014 no maintained external vocabulary covers these behavioral header facets. MIME body-part metadata terms (MultipartBodyPart, InlinePart, MultipartType, ContentDisposition, ContentTransferEncoding, hasMultipartType, hasInlinePart, hasContentDisposition, hasContentTransferEncoding, partId, contentId, charset; the design) are canonical \u2014 no maintained external RDF vocabulary covers granular MIME structure, Content-ID, transfer encoding, or disposition values. Mailbox hierarchy terms (parentMailbox, childMailbox, mailboxSortOrder, mailboxPath, mailboxTotalMessages, mailboxUnreadMessages; the design) are canonical \u2014 JMAP (RFC 8621) has no maintained RDF vocabulary. parentMailbox/childMailbox specialize the universal partOf/hasPart spine; path and counts are derived projection state (Principle 12). Calendar invitation bridge terms (describesEvent, calendarAttachment, calendarUid, CalendarMethod, hasCalendarMethod, messageKindCalendarInvitation; mail-corpus invitation consumer) are canonical \u2014 no maintained external RDF vocabulary covers the email\u2192event bridge. iCalendar METHOD/UID alignments are by reference to icaltzd. Email versioning terms (EmailPatchDiff, hasPatchDiff, messageIdGenerated, messageIdCollision, canonicalFingerprint, bodyLineFingerprint, analysisScope, analysisInputBodyLine; the design) are canonical \u2014 no maintained external vocabulary covers Message-ID collision tracking, body-line fingerprinting, or email patch-diff artifacts. Canonical/variant status is represented via the cross-cutting VersionMembership relator from versions.ttl, not as email-specific subclasses. JMAP structural identifier terms (blobId, bodyStructure, BodyValue; the design) are canonical \u2014 JMAP (RFC 8620/8621) defines blobId, partId, and BodyStructure at the protocol level, but has no maintained RDF vocabulary. bodyStructure is a serialized projection; the canonical MIME tree is the existing hasBodyPart/hasPart spine (Principle 4)."
